bottom_line: Nvidia's boss drama whipsawed the whole market: his return sent Nvidia up 31% and gave the Nasdaq its best day since April 2025, then tech gave part of it back Tuesday. Under that noise, the bigger money story is that inflation pressure hasn't gone away, and some big names warn the Fed could raise rates again in December.

stories.title: Nvidia's CEO is back
stories.real: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO after admitting an extramarital affair, then was reinstated days later. Nvidia shares jumped 31% and the company added almost $1tn in value, lifting the tech-heavy Nasdaq 6.5%. On Tuesday the stock fell over 5% and dragged tech down with it. The investigations aren't over: Nvidia still faces an internal probe and California and federal scrutiny. Trump said he 'convinced' Nvidia to bring Huang back, and members of Congress from both parties are pushing back.
stories.you: One company now moves the whole market, so if you own an index fund, one CEO's scandal can swing your account up or down in a single day.

stories.title: Inflation isn't done, rates may rise
stories.real: The WSJ reports cost pressures already building up that point to higher inflation, partly from oil. Some voices expect the Fed (the people who set interest rates) to raise rates again in December, and Bill Ackman warned a move on December 9 could trigger a recession. Meanwhile, business activity growth slowed in November, and commercial real estate activity fell 14% in October as rates rose. At the same time, hiring sped up in October.
stories.you: If rates go up again, loans, credit cards and mortgages stay expensive. Prices may keep climbing faster than you'd like.

stories.title: Shoppers feel better, but not fully
stories.real: Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 after the midterms, with election uncertainty over and gas prices falling. People still worry about inflation, and Thanksgiving travelers, a near-record number, are paying more because of fuel costs. Best Buy said same-store sales grew 6.1%, its best in five years.
stories.you: People are spending again, but everyday costs like travel are still biting.

stories.title: Hot tech names are cooling
stories.real: Anthropic fell 12% and is now below its $83 IPO price, after opening at $111.50 on Nov. 19. Analog Devices dropped 7.6%, Dell 5.9%, and HPE slipped on a weak profit-margin forecast. Some headlines say the market has entered a correction (a drop of about a tenth from the high).
stories.you: A buzzy new stock can trade below its starting price within days, and hype does not protect you from losses.

stories.title: Big drug company deal
stories.real: Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed in pharma's biggest deal in three years, and Insmed shares rose 14%. Sanofi needs new revenue because its top drugs will soon face cheaper generic competition.
stories.you: When big drug patents run out, generics can make those medicines cheaper, and drugmakers go shopping to replace the lost sales.
